Algebra I · Lesson 4.2

Solving Linear Equations

Solve this lesson →All lessons

In 4.1 a check settled any candidate. Substitute, evaluate both sides, compare. What it never did was produce a candidate. This lesson builds the producer, a way to trade an equation for a simpler equation with exactly the same solutions, and the first trade is one you can already make.

Problem
The equation w+24=63w+24=63 is true at exactly one value of ww, and at that value its two sides are the same number. Take 2424 away from that number on each side. On the left this leaves ww alone. Enter the number the right side becomes.
Show a hint
  • At the solution both sides are one number. Taking the same amount from each copy of that number leaves equal amounts.
  • Subtracting 2424 from the left side leaves ww alone. Do the identical subtraction to the 6363.
Show the full solution
63−24=3963−24=39, so the right side becomes 3939​. The new equation reads w=39w=39, and the check 39+24=6339+24=63 confirms it. That one subtraction solved the equation.
Key idea
Do the same thing to both sides. If an equation is true at some value, its two sides are the same number there, and adding or subtracting the same amount on both sides keeps them the same number. So the move never destroys a solution. It also reverses, since subtracting what was added restores the original equation, so the argument runs backward too and no new solutions appear. The two equations are true at exactly the same values. Equations related this way are called equivalent, and every legal solving move produces an equivalent equation.
Problem
Solve t−38=26t−38=26. One balance move does it, adding 3838 to both sides removes the subtraction and leaves tt alone. Check your value in the original equation, the 4.1 way, before entering it.
Show a hint
  • Undo the subtraction with the opposite move, made on both sides.
  • Adding 3838 to both sides leaves tt alone. The right side becomes 26+3826+38.
Show the full solution
Add 3838 to both sides, t=26+38=64t=26+38=64​. Check, 64−38=2664−38=26. The check costs seconds and catches every slip.

The same argument covers scaling. At a solution both sides are one number, tripling that number on each side keeps the sides equal, and dividing by 33 undoes it. It looks like any multiplier works. One of them does not, and the next problem finds it.

Problem
The equation 6d=846d=84 is true only at d=14d=14. Multiply both sides by 00 and every term collapses, leaving 0=00=0. Test the values −3−3, 00, 88, 1414, and 2020 in the new equation. Enter how many of them are solutions of the new equation but not of the original.
Show a hint
  • The new equation never mentions dd, so ask which values could possibly fail it.
  • All five values satisfy 0=00=0, and the original is satisfied only at 1414. Count the values that pass one equation but not the other.
Show the full solution
Every value makes 0=00=0 true, and only 1414 satisfies 6d=846d=84, so 44​ of the five are new. Multiplying by zero manufactured solutions, and nothing undoes it, since dividing by zero is not a move.
Key idea
Multiply or divide both sides by any nonzero number. At a solution the sides are one number, scaling both copies by cc keeps them equal, and dividing by cc reverses the move, so no solutions are gained or lost. The reverse step is what makes the move legal, and zero has no reverse step. Multiplying by zero turns any equation into 0=00=0, true for every value, and there is no dividing by zero to get back. A legal move must be reversible.
Problem
Solve 12m=13212m=132. The left side is twelve copies of mm, so divide both sides by 1212. Check the value before entering it.
Show a hint
  • Division is the reverse of the multiplication that built the left side.
  • Dividing both sides by 1212 leaves mm alone against 132132 divided by 1212.
Show the full solution
Divide both sides by 1212, m=13212=11m=12132​=11​. Check, 12⋅11=13212⋅11=132.
Problem
Solve n15=815n​=8 by multiplying both sides by 1515. Check the value in the original equation before entering it.
Show a hint
  • The left side divided nn by 1515, so undo it with the opposite scaling move.
  • Multiplying both sides by 1515 leaves nn alone. The right side becomes 88 times 1515.
Show the full solution
Multiply both sides by 1515, n=8⋅15=120n=8⋅15=120​. Check, 12015=815120​=8.

In 4.1 you read 9x+7=529x+7=52 with no method at all. The term 9x9x had to be 4545, and dividing by 99 finishes it, x=5x=5. That reading was really two balance moves, subtract 77 from both sides, then divide both sides by 99. The left side was built by multiplying and then adding, so it unwinds in the opposite order.

Problem
Solve 3a+29=983a+29=98. Subtract first to expose the term 3a3a, then divide. Check your value in the original equation before entering it.
Show a hint
  • The 2929 sits outside the product 3a3a, so it is the last thing that happened and the first thing to undo.
  • Subtracting 2929 from both sides gives 3a=693a=69.
Show the full solution
Subtract 2929 from both sides, 3a=693a=69, then divide by 33, a=23a=23​. Check, 3⋅23+29=983⋅23+29=98.
Key idea
Undo the last operation first. In 3a+29=983a+29=98 the left side multiplied aa by 33 and then added 2929, so the 2929 sits outside the product. Subtracting it exposes 3a3a, and dividing exposes aa. Dividing by 33 first is legal too, it just drags fractions in, a+293=983a+329​=398​. Unwinding from the outside in, last operation undone first, keeps the numbers whole as long as possible.
Problem
Solve 10y+74=8210y+74=82. The moves are the same as before, and the answer is not a whole number. Enter it as a fraction in lowest terms.
Show a hint
  • Nothing about the moves needs the answer to be whole. Unwind as usual.
  • Subtracting 7474 gives 10y=810y=8. Divide and reduce.
Show the full solution
Subtract 7474, 10y=810y=8, divide by 1010, y=810=45y=108​=54​​. Check, 10⋅45+74=8+74=8210⋅54​+74=8+74=82. Fractional solutions are normal outcomes, not signs of a mistake.

Sometimes a side needs cleanup before any unwinding. When the variable side is a pile of like terms, combine them the 2.4 way first. After that the equation is two-step and the moves are the ones you already have.

Problem
Solve 16q+27−8q+13=10016q+27−8q+13=100. Combine like terms on the left before making any balance move. Enter the solution as a fraction in lowest terms.
Show a hint
  • The left side is not two-step yet. Collect the qq terms and the constants first.
  • 16q−8q=8q16q−8q=8q and 27+13=4027+13=40, so the equation is 8q+40=1008q+40=100.
Show the full solution
Combining gives 8q+40=1008q+40=100, so 8q=608q=60 and q=608=152q=860​=215​​. Check, 8⋅152+40=60+40=1008⋅215​+40=60+40=100.
Problem
Solve 34c=5143​c=51. One move does it, multiply both sides by the reciprocal 4334​, the 2.5 skill. Enter the solution.
Show a hint
  • A fractional coefficient clears in one move, scaling by the number that multiplies with it to 11.
  • c=51⋅43c=51⋅34​. Divide 5151 by 33 before multiplying.
Show the full solution
Multiply both sides by 4334​, c=51⋅43=68c=51⋅34​=68​. Check, 34⋅68=5143​⋅68=51.
Problem
Solve 28−x=9328−x=93. Subtracting 2828 from both sides leaves −x=65−x=65, a statement about the opposite of xx. One more move finishes it. Enter the solution.
Show a hint
  • −x−x means (−1)x(−1)x, and −1−1 is a nonzero number like any other.
  • Divide both sides of −x=65−x=65 by −1−1, or read it directly, the opposite of xx is 6565.
Show the full solution
Subtract 2828, −x=65−x=65, then multiply both sides by −1−1, x=−65x=−65​. Check, 28−(−65)=28+65=9328−(−65)=28+65=93. If the opposite of xx is 6565, then xx is −65−65, the moves and the reading agree.
Fun fact
Around 820, al-Khwarizmi of Baghdad wrote a book on solving equations whose title word al-jabr, restoring, meant carrying a subtracted quantity to the other side. Latin translations kept the word, and it became algebra.
Problem
A student solves 5x+30=805x+30=80 by erasing the 3030 from the left side only, getting 5x=805x=80 and then x=16x=16. Check that candidate the 4.1 way. Evaluate the left side at x=16x=16 and enter how much it overshoots the right side.
Show a hint
  • A check needs no opinion about the moves. Substitute the candidate and evaluate the original left side.
  • At x=16x=16 the left side is 5(16)+305(16)+30. Compare that with 8080.
Show the full solution
The left side at 1616 is 5⋅16+30=1105⋅16+30=110, and 110−80=30110−80=30​, exactly the 3030 that left one side but not the other. Legal moves hit both sides. Subtracting 3030 from both gives 5x=505x=50, so x=10x=10, and 5⋅10+30=805⋅10+30=80 checks.
Problem
Solve 35h+46=2253​h+46=22. Undo the addition first, then multiply by the reciprocal. The solution is negative, and the check still takes ten seconds. Enter the solution.
Show a hint
  • Last operation first. The 4646 was added after the coefficient did its work.
  • Subtracting 4646 gives 35h=−2453​h=−24. Multiply by 5335​.
Show the full solution
Subtract 4646, 35h=−2453​h=−24, multiply by 5335​, h=−24⋅53=−40h=−24⋅35​=−40​. Check, 35(−40)+46=−24+46=2253​(−40)+46=−24+46=22.

Every equation in this lesson kept its variable on one side, and four reversible moves handled all of them. 4.3 starts where that stops, equations with the variable on both sides, and the balance principle carries over unchanged.

Practice these ideas

Practice
Enter the solution of x+34=59x+34=59.
Show the solution
Subtract 3434 from both sides, x=59−34=25x=59−34=25​. Check, 25+34=5925+34=59, so the value passes the 4.1 test.
Practice
Enter the solution of y−27=44y−27=44.
Show the solution
Add 2727 to both sides, y=44+27=71y=44+27=71​. Check, 71−27=4471−27=44.
Practice
Enter the solution of 7k=1197k=119.
Show the solution
Divide both sides by 77, k=1197=17k=7119​=17​. Check, 7⋅17=1197⋅17=119.
Practice
Enter the solution of t9=129t​=12.
Show the solution
Multiply both sides by 99, t=12⋅9=108t=12⋅9=108​. Check, 1089=129108​=12.
Practice
Enter the solution of w+53=35w+53=35.
Show the solution
Subtract 5353 from both sides, w=35−53=−18w=35−53=−18​. Check, −18+53=35−18+53=35. Subtracting from both sides works the same even when the result is negative.
Practice
Enter the solution of 2k+41=792k+41=79.
Show the solution
Subtract 4141, 2k=382k=38, then divide by 22, k=19k=19​. Check, 2⋅19+41=38+41=792⋅19+41=38+41=79.
Practice
Enter the solution of 6p+61=136p+61=13.
Show the solution
Subtract 6161, 6p=13−61=−486p=13−61=−48, then divide by 66, p=−8p=−8​. Check, 6(−8)+61=−48+61=136(−8)+61=−48+61=13.
Practice
Enter the solution of k12+5=812k​+5=8.
Show the solution
Subtract 55, k12=312k​=3, then multiply both sides by 1212, k=36k=36​. Check, 3612+5=3+5=81236​+5=3+5=8.
Practice
Combine like terms first, then solve 13w+12−8w+73=17513w+12−8w+73=175. Enter the solution.
Show the solution
Combining gives 5w+85=1755w+85=175, so 5w=905w=90 and w=18w=18​. Check, 13⋅18+12−8⋅18+73=234+12−144+73=17513⋅18+12−8⋅18+73=234+12−144+73=175. Combining is not a balance move at all, it rewrites one side into an equal expression, so nothing on the other side changes.
Practice
Solve 2(u+67)=2322(u+67)=232, distributing once the 2.1 way or dividing both sides by 22 first. Enter the solution.
Show the solution
Divide both sides by 22, u+67=116u+67=116, then subtract 6767, u=49u=49​. Check, 2(49+67)=2⋅116=2322(49+67)=2⋅116=232. Distributing first gives 2u+134=2322u+134=232 and lands on the same value.
Practice
Enter the solution of 23g=5832​g=58.
Show the solution
Multiply both sides by 3223​, g=58⋅32=29⋅3=87g=58⋅23​=29⋅3=87​. Check, 23⋅87=5832​⋅87=58.
Practice
Enter the solution of −12u=72−12u=72.
Show the solution
Divide both sides by −12−12, u=72−12=−6u=−1272​=−6​. Check, −12⋅(−6)=72−12⋅(−6)=72. A positive product from a negative coefficient forces a negative solution.
Practice
Enter the solution of 66−x=14566−x=145.
Show the solution
Subtract 6666, −x=79−x=79, then multiply both sides by −1−1, x=−79x=−79​. Check, 66−(−79)=66+79=14566−(−79)=66+79=145.
Practice
Solve 8n+77=868n+77=86. Enter the solution as a fraction in lowest terms.
Show the solution
Subtract 7777, 8n=98n=9, then divide by 88, n=98n=89​​. Check, 8⋅98+77=9+77=868⋅89​+77=9+77=86. A fractional answer is a normal outcome, not a sign of a slip.
Practice
To solve 3x−21=993x−21=99, a student divides the 3x3x and the 9999 by 33 but leaves the −21−21 alone, writing x−21=33x−21=33, so x=54x=54. Check that candidate the 4.1 way. Evaluate the left side of the original equation at x=54x=54 and enter how much it exceeds the right side.
Show the solution
The left side at 5454 is 3⋅54−21=162−21=1413⋅54−21=162−21=141, and 141−99=42141−99=42​. Dividing both sides means every term, x−7=33x−7=33, or add 2121 first to get 3x=1203x=120. Either way x=40x=40, and 3⋅40−21=993⋅40−21=99 checks.
Practice
Combine like terms first, then solve 3m+32−4m+57=963m+32−4m+57=96. Enter the solution.
Show the solution
Combining gives −m+89=96−m+89=96, so −m=7−m=7 and m=−7m=−7​. Check, 3(−7)+32−4(−7)+57=−21+32+28+57=963(−7)+32−4(−7)+57=−21+32+28+57=96. A net coefficient of −1−1 reads as the opposite of mm, so mm is the opposite of 77.
Practice
Solve 83n=−1438​n=−14. Enter the solution as a fraction in lowest terms.
Show the solution
Multiply both sides by 3883​, n=−14⋅38=−428=−214n=−14⋅83​=−842​=−421​​. Check, 83⋅(−214)=−16812=−1438​⋅(−421​)=−12168​=−14. Multiplying by the positive number 3883​ does not change the sign, so the solution stays negative.
